assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Yongle has a single persona and it is planned here. The gate is a Population threshold, not a turn: each city crosses on its own, the plan tracks every city separately, and the yields stay flat until the first one does. That flatline is expected.

verdict.one_line: Grow four river cities on Granaries, Aqueducts and Farms before running a single project, then push them over Population 10 one at a time with the Lijia Food project and turn each crossing into a University and a Researcher. Nothing happens for eighty turns, and then the Science chart turns.
verdict.why: Lijia pays per Citizen and pays most in large cities, and the Lijia projects turn Production into the Food or Gold that carries a city over the line, so the kit rewards a few very big cities and nothing else. Dynastic Cycle makes every boost worth an extra tenth, and the growth path triggers an unusual number of them: Irrigation, Construction, Military Engineering, Feudalism, Civil Service and Urbanization all come from building Housing and growing the city. Science is the verdict because per-Citizen Science stacks with Campuses, Pingala's Researcher promotion and Rationalism in exactly the cities the gate produces. The kit has no offensive lever, only a defensive ranged unit and a wall, and no Faith engine, so the Great Wall's Culture and Tourism and the per-Citizen Culture are the second line rather than the first.

must_have: Fresh water at the capital and at two or three more city sites within about eight tiles, because Population 10 needs Housing that only rivers, lakes, Granaries and Aqueducts supply before the Industrial era.
At least two Luxury resources of different types inside the first four cities' reach, or Amenities stop the cities before Housing does.
prefer: Grassland and plains along the rivers with Wheat, Rice or Cattle, so the Farms and Pastures that feed the threshold also give half a Housing each.
Mountains beside the capital's Campus tile, for Natural Philosophy adjacency and the Astronomy Eureka.
A narrow land border with the nearest rival, so a short Great Wall line and one walled city are the whole defensive floor.
Hong Kong, Mohenjo-Daro or Mitla within reach of the Scout; each pays this plan more than any other city-state.
map_check.no_go: There is no hard no-go, only a soft one: a dry, cold or desert start with no river or lake for three cities. Every city then starts with a third of the Housing, needs an Aqueduct before it can grow past six, and crosses the threshold so late that the per-Citizen yields arrive after rivals have caught up in Population.
map_check.fallback: On dry or cold land, play China as a Dynastic Cycle Science civilization: chase every Eureka and Inspiration, build Classical and Medieval wonders for the free boosts, put a Campus in every city, and treat Lijia as an Industrial-era bonus that switches on when Neighborhoods and Sewers supply the Housing the land never did.

kit_levers.name: Lijia
kit_levers.buys: Lijia projects in every city that turn a share of the city's Production into Food, Faith or Gold, and extra Gold, Science and Culture per Citizen in large cities.
kit_levers.exploit: The projects are a growth tool, not an income. Run the Food version in the one city closest to the next threshold, only while it has Housing and Amenities to hold the extra Citizen, and switch back to a building the turn it crosses. A city at 10 is worth more than two at 6 because the per-Citizen yields only pay large cities, so the plan grows four big cities rather than eight small ones and tracks each against the threshold on its own.

kit_levers.name: Dynastic Cycle
kit_levers.buys: Eurekas and Inspirations pay an extra tenth of the cost, and completing a wonder grants a free Eureka and a free Inspiration.
kit_levers.exploit: The growth path triggers more boosts than most plans: the Farm, the Water Mill, the Aqueduct, six Farms, the first city at 10 and the first at 15 are all Eurekas or Inspirations. Research nothing unboosted that a Farm or an Aqueduct would boost a few turns later, and take one growth wonder an era (Hanging Gardens, Colosseum, Forbidden City, Ruhr Valley) so the free boosts cover what the plan cannot trigger.

kit_levers.name: Crouching Tiger Cannon
kit_levers.buys: A Medieval ranged unit at Machinery with 50 Ranged Strength and range 1, needing no strategic resource.
kit_levers.exploit: The defensive floor for an empire that never builds an army. Two in the border city behind the Great Wall, with the three Archers that gave the Machinery Eureka still garrisoned, stop a Medieval rush without an Encampment, and the garrisons are what Retainers counts for Amenities.

kit_levers.name: Great Wall
kit_levers.buys: A border improvement at Masonry with Gold, more for each adjacent segment, Culture once Castles is researched, Tourism after Flight, and a defensive bonus for units standing on it.
kit_levers.exploit: Lay a continuous line of three or more segments on the border facing the most aggressive neighbour, on tiles the growing cities will never farm. It is the defensive floor that lets the Production go into Granaries and Aqueducts instead of Walls, Gold for the treasury Yinding wants positive now, and the Culture and Tourism line behind the Science verdict later.

kit_levers.name: Yinding
kit_levers.buys: Yongle likes civilizations running a positive Gold income and dislikes those running a deficit.
kit_levers.exploit: Irrelevant to your own play, but a reminder to keep your own treasury positive: the Gold version of Lijia and the Great Wall are what pay for the Housing buildings bought ahead of each crossing. An AI Yongle on the same map will race you for river land and big cities, so settle the shared rivers first.

gate.gate_condition: The first city reaches Population 10 with a completed Lijia Food project as the step that carries it over, and it has the Housing and Amenities to stay there: Housing at 11 or more and Amenities at zero or better on the turn it crosses. Not a turn number: every city crosses on its own, the threshold sheet tracks each one, and the post-gate phase opens in a city the turn that city crosses.
staging: Housing two above Population in the city about to cross: river or lake, Granary, Aqueduct and four or more Farms or Pastures, checked on the threshold sheet the turn the project starts.
Amenities at zero or better after the extra Citizen: two luxury types connected, Classical Republic adopted, and the Arena built or a third luxury traded in.
A Campus with a Library in the city about to cross and Education within ten turns, so the University and the per-Citizen Science land together.
Pingala appointed in the capital with a governor title unspent, so Researcher is taken the turn the capital crosses rather than ten turns later.
The next city to cross named on the sheet, with its Granary built and its Aqueduct under way, so the project moves across without a gap.
Hong Kong's suzerainty if it is on the map, or envoys flowing toward it, for the extra Production on every Lijia turn.
A defensive floor that needs no attention: Ancient Walls and two Archers in each border city and a line of three Great Wall segments facing the nearest rival.
gate.late_gate: If no city has crossed by turn 120, twenty turns behind pace, Housing is almost always the cause, not Production. Stop every project, put the capital's Builders on Farms and Pastures, finish the Aqueduct, send two Traders from the other cities into the capital for Food, and appoint Magnus with Surplus Logistics there. If Amenities are the cause, trade for a luxury an AI has spare, build the Arena, and slot Retainers with an Archer garrisoned in the city. Do not settle more cities during the delay, since each one splits the luxuries further, and do not start a second city's project to make up time: two half-housed cities cross later than one fully housed one. If the delay runs past turn 140, the gate is no longer the bottleneck and the abort applies.
gate.closing_window: The Lijia yields are permanent, so the far deadline is not the ability expiring but parity in Population and Science. Through the Renaissance the AI's cities stall at eight to twelve for want of Housing, and China's crossed cities are three to six Citizens larger, which is the whole lead. Parity arrives in the Industrial era, roughly turn 170 to 200 on Emperor, when rivals build Neighborhoods and Sewers and their capitals reach the same size without projects, and in Science when the leading rival's Research Labs come in. Convert before that: every core city over 10 with a University by turn 170, the capital at 15 with Urbanization in reach, and Science per turn first on the table at the turn 190 check. After parity the projects are worth running only for Gold; a project turn in a city past 15 is a Research Lab turn lost.

phases.name: Found on fresh water
phases.objective: State the gate on turn 1, settle the capital and two more cities on rivers or lakes, found Fertility Rites, and have Pottery, Irrigation and Craftsmanship in, so every city has a Granary queued and its Farm tiles improved before the Classical era begins.

build_order.why: Find the river and lake sites for the next three cities and the city-states this plan wants, Hong Kong and Mohenjo-Daro above all; the first civilization met is the Writing Eureka.
Archery Eureka on a barbarian scout, and the capital's only defender until the Walls.
Second city on a river or lake within six tiles; fresh water is the cheapest Housing in the game and the gate needs it.
Farm Wheat or Rice for the Irrigation Eureka, then two more improved tiles for Craftsmanship; each Farm is also half a Housing.
Culture toward Early Empire and Political Philosophy; Classical Republic is the government this plan runs until the Renaissance.
Third city on fresh water; the gate wants three river cities more than five dry ones.
The first Housing building, in the capital before it reaches five Population.

research.note: Granary, the first Housing building; no boost, so research it first and plain.
Farms on Wheat and Rice and the Hanging Gardens; Eureka from the first Farm on a resource.
Mines for the capital's Production and The Wheel's Eureka; no boost.
Campus; Eureka free from the first civilization met.
Archers are the garrison and later the Machinery Eureka; Eureka from the Slinger kill.

civics.note: Urban Planning while there are two cities; no Inspiration exists.
Ilkum for the Builders that farm the river; Inspiration from three improved tiles.
The Trader and the road to Early Empire; research it plain.

policies.why: Production in every city while they build Settlers and Granaries.
The Slinger and the starting Warrior beat barbarian scouts near the capital.
Swap in for Urban Planning while Builders are queued; the Farms are the Housing and the Feudalism Inspiration both.

pantheon.why: Faster growth in every city and a free Builder to farm the second resource; Population is this plan's whole currency.

city_states.why: Every city gets full fresh-water Housing as if beside a river; worth the first envoys if met.
Hong Kong is the one to look for: Production toward city projects, which is every Lijia turn the plan will run.

checkpoints.test: Three cities on fresh water, Fertility Rites founded, a Granary in the capital, and Irrigation and Craftsmanship done?
checkpoints.pass: Enter the Housing phase; start the capital's Campus and the threshold sheet for each city.
checkpoints.fail: A city off fresh water moves its Granary to the front of its queue and is marked last to cross. If Fertility Rites was taken, found City Patron Goddess; if Irrigation is late, farm anyway and the Eureka follows.

tasks.text: Write the gate down: the strategy opens when a city crosses Population 10 on a Lijia Food project with the Housing and Amenities to hold it. Settle the capital on a river or lake.
Scout for river and lake sites; record each as a future city with its fresh water, Farm tiles and luxury.
Farm the first Wheat or Rice beside the capital; Irrigation Eureka collected.
Second city settled on fresh water within six tiles of the capital.
Found Fertility Rites; the free Builder farms the second resource.
Third city settled on fresh water; Granary first in its queue after a Monument.

phases.name: Housing before projects
phases.objective: Build the Housing and Amenities the gate assumes but does not provide: Granaries everywhere, Water Mills on the rivers, Farms in clusters, a Campus with a Library and an Aqueduct in the capital, two luxury types connected and Classical Republic adopted, behind Ancient Walls and a Great Wall line on the threatened border. No Lijia project runs yet. Every yield graph is flat in this phase, and that is the plan working, not failing.

build_order.why: Capital, beside Mountains; the first district gives State Workforce, and its Library is what the per-Citizen Science multiplies after the gate.
In every new city before it reaches five Population; Housing first, everything else second.
Every river city; growth and the Construction Eureka.
Fourth city on fresh water. Four cities that each reach ten are worth more to this kit than eight that stop at six.
Farms in clusters along the rivers; six of them are the Feudalism Inspiration and each is half a Housing.
In the border city facing the nearest rival; the Engineering Eureka and the floor while the Production goes into Housing.
Capital, the turn Engineering lands; the Housing the threshold needs and the Military Engineering Eureka.
In the capital's Campus; Great Scientist points and the building the gate city must have before it crosses.

The gate check is run per city; the post-gate economy starts in the capital while the others are still staging.

checkpoints.fail: If only the capital has crossed, the second city lacks Housing, not Production: buy its Aqueduct or Granary with Gold-project Gold and run nothing else there until it is in.

tasks.text: Start the Lijia Food project in the capital and nowhere else.

decision_triggers.name: Housing cap under a project
decision_triggers.if: A city running a Lijia project comes within one of its Housing.
decision_triggers.then: Stop the project that turn. Build or buy the Granary, Aqueduct or Neighborhood, farm the next tile, and restart only when Housing is two above Population.

decision_triggers.name: Amenities would go negative
decision_triggers.if: The next Citizen would put a city's Amenities below zero.
decision_triggers.then: No project there. Connect or trade for a luxury, garrison a unit under Retainers, build the Arena, or move the project to a city with Amenities to spare.

decision_triggers.name: Neighbour arms before the gate
decision_triggers.if: A neighbour moves several units to the border before the capital has crossed.
decision_triggers.then: Buy Ancient Walls in the border city, add Great Wall segments in the path and two Archers or Crouching Tigers; do not pull the capital off its Housing builds and run no project in the border city until the threat passes.

decision_triggers.name: Which Lijia to run
decision_triggers.if: A city has crossed, has Housing for one more Citizen, and nothing urgent is left to build.
decision_triggers.then: Food if it is still below the next target of 15; Gold if it sits at its Housing or Amenity cap; Faith only when a Great Scientist or Naturalist is waiting to be bought with it.

decision_triggers.name: Science rival at parity
decision_triggers.if: At any ten-turn check after turn 150 a rival's Science per turn exceeds China's by a tenth.
decision_triggers.then: Stop the Food project in every crossed city; Universities and Industrial Zones first, the Gold project to buy them, and a Research Alliance with the nearest friendly civilization.

abort.trigger: No city has crossed Population 10 by turn 140 and the capital is at its Housing cap with no Aqueduct, Granary or Farm left to build, or a rival already out-researches China by a third.
actions: Stop every Lijia project; they are Production with nothing to grow into.
Play China as a Dynastic Cycle civilization: chase every Eureka and Inspiration, build Medieval and Renaissance wonders for the free boosts, and put a Campus in every city.
Settle a fifth and sixth city on whatever land is left, since the tall premise is gone, and aim for Culture through the Great Wall's Tourism or for Score.

fail_state: Turn 150 with four cities at Population 7 to 9, Lijia projects run in all of them at once into full Housing so every Citizen grew at a fraction of the normal rate, no Universities because the Production went into projects, and the per-Citizen yields never switched on. China is then a small Science civilization with good boosts and an empty treasury, an era behind the leader, and the gate never opened in a city that could use it.
common_mistakes: Running Lijia projects in every city from the Classical era. A project turn is a Granary or Aqueduct turn lost, and a city at its Housing cap grows slowly no matter how much Food the project makes.
Reading the flat first eighty turns as failure and switching plans. The yields are threshold-gated; the pre-gate phase is supposed to look like nothing.
Settling off fresh water for a resource. A dry city starts with a fraction of the Housing and needs an Aqueduct before it can even approach the threshold.
Solving Housing and forgetting Amenities. A city at 10 needs several Amenities, and a city that crosses into unhappiness loses the yields the crossing was for.
Leaving the project running after the city crosses. The turn it reaches 10, the city switches to its University and Pingala takes Researcher; the project moves to the next city on the sheet.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset with the Leader Pass (China, Yongle, Lijia, Dynastic Cycle, Crouching Tiger, Great Wall). The civ-info text calls the Crouching Tiger Cannon a Bombard replacement that needs no Niter; in the game the Crouching Tiger is a standalone Medieval ranged unit at Machinery with range 1 and no resource cost, and the plan follows the game. The civ-info places the Great Wall on Hills; in the game it is built along the border at Masonry, with Gold per adjacent segment, Culture at Castles and Tourism at Flight, and the plan follows the game.

Lijia is taken as the civ-info describes it: projects converting a share of Production into Food, Faith or Gold, and extra Gold, Science and Culture per Citizen in large cities. The Population 10 threshold is the repository's Gate supplement for Yongle; exact Lijia percentages and per-Citizen values are not quoted and should be read off the in-game Civilopedia.
Boost objectives cross-checked against civilization6planner.com tech-tree and civics-tree pages, 2026-10-02.

Leadership Focus tags, caveats and Gate supplement for Yongle in this repository; the Gate template sets Housing and food before project spam, per-city threshold tracking and an explicit note that the pre-threshold flatline is expected.
